rollback_note.who_runs_a_restore: A person under the sign-off. The mode never restores, deletes or retries.
rollback_note.from_what: The captured version ids in the --capture file the sign-off named: per listed date {data:{etag,version_id}, manifest:{etag,version_id}}; plus sidecar {etag,version_id} and method_row {data,manifest} when the served sidecar / method row differed from the new build's (the mode refuses to start otherwise). Each restore is a copy of the captured version onto its key (S3 CopyObject with the source VersionId), which makes a new latest version and removes nothing.
rollback_note.quoted_from_the_mode_help_text (REMINT_H: DELETES NOTHING and does not roll back: the bucket keeps versions; rollback is a copy of the captured version id, done by a person under the sign-off
rollback_note.quoted_from_the_mode_comment_block (data: It deletes nothing and does not roll back; the bucket keeps versions, and a rollback is a copy of the captured version id, done by a person under the sign-off.
rollback_note.quoted_from_the_mode_failure_output (_re: nothing was deleted and no rollback was attempted; N key(s) were written or attempted before this stopped (roll back from the capture, by a person under the sign-off):
rollback_note.capture_covers_every_key_touched: Yes for every failure point the tests inject, as the mode defines the capture: a day is in the capture whenever it is listed (required); the sidecar and the method row are written only if they differ from the new build's, and the mode refuses to start in that case unless the capture names them. So a key the mode can write is always a key the capture names. Not covered: a key written by something other than the mode.

not_established: Behaviour against the real bucket: no AWS call was made. That the bucket is versioned, that the captured version ids exist there, and that a CopyObject of a captured VersionId restores the key byte for byte were not exercised (the fake keeps every version; the real bucket's versioning state is the sign-off's to confirm).

A real process kill, an OS signal, or a kill DURING a put: F8 is the state when an uncaught BaseException is raised by the nth put (puts 1..n-1 landed). S3 makes a single put whole-or-absent; this is a statement about S3, not something the tests show.
A put that is retried by the SDK or that stores and then times out: F10 is the stored-then-raise case through the writer's ETag check; other timing shapes are not modelled.

A second writer to the table during the run: the mode compares the capture with the served heads once, before the writes; a write by anything else between that check and the puts is not detected and not tested.
Local leftovers after a kill (stream_parquet temp files under the system temp directory).
A malformed manifest.json on read-back (json.loads raising inside the try) is caught by the same handler as F4/F11 and prints 'writing <date> stopped: ...'; not given its own test.
The order in which a person restores the keys of a half pair: the restore itself passes through states in which a pair is half; not examined.

Whether the data that a restore returns is the data the served table showed at the capture: the capture holds ETag and version id, and the mode checks both at the start; the content behind the version id was not re-read.
